## How these widgets work

Each tool uses a compact control panel and linked visual panels. Controls use
seeded samples: changing a setting and returning to it reproduces the same
draws, while **Generate another sample** advances to a new sample.

Use the staged reveal: ask students to predict the interpretation, loss basin,
or interval before pressing the reveal button. Hover observations to inspect
their fitted values and residuals.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {
  coefficientLab,
  regressionLab,
  predictionIntervalLab,
} from "./regression-lab.js"
```

## Coefficients — what do α and β mean?

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
coefficientLab({ Inputs, Plot })
```

::: {.rl-slide-note}
Ask: what is the predicted mean at x = 0? What happens to the predicted mean
when x increases by one?
:::

## Least squares — where is the smallest MSE?

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
regressionLab({ Inputs, Plot })
```

::: {.rl-slide-note}
Ask students to move the line toward the darkest part of the MSE landscape,
then reveal the exact least-squares solution.
:::

## Confidence interval or prediction interval?

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
predictionIntervalLab({ Inputs, Plot })
```

::: {.rl-slide-note}
Ask: are we estimating the mean response or predicting one new outcome? What
changes near the edge of the observed x-range?
:::
